checklist.name: intellectual disability
quotes: may include any of these manifestations: intellectual disability
the vast majority of subjects with SSADHD have intellectual disabilities
checklist.why: Listed first among the core features and described as present in the vast majority.

checklist.name: speech or language impairment
quotes: intellectual disability, language difficulties
prominent expressive language impairment
better receptive than expressive language functions
checklist.why: Core feature; the review stresses expressive more than receptive deficits.

checklist.name: hypotonia
quotes: language difficulties, hypotonia, motor function deficits
checklist.why: Named among the most consistently reported signs (Statement 3).

checklist.name: gross or fine motor deficits
quotes: The majority of SSADHD individuals have gross and fine motor deficits
checklist.why: Described as present in the majority.

checklist.name: seizures or epilepsy
quotes: Seizures in SSADHD are predominantly generalized but may be focal in onset
epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
checklist.why: Core feature; severity said to worsen with age.

checklist.name: EEG abnormality (background slowing or epileptiform activity)
quotes: The most common EEG patterns seen in SSADHD are generalized (diffuse) background slowing and focal or multifocal epileptiform activity
EEGs may also be abnormal in individuals with SSADHD who do not have seizures
checklist.why: Physiological finding the review says can occur without seizures, so it is separate from epilepsy.

checklist.name: ataxia
quotes: movement disorders (such as ataxia, dystonia, and exertional dyskinesia)
checklist.why: Named movement disorder among the main clinical features.

checklist.name: dystonia
quotes: movement disorders (such as ataxia, dystonia, and exertional dyskinesia)
with dystonic posturing or hemiballismus
checklist.why: Named movement disorder among the main clinical features.

checklist.name: exertional dyskinesia
quotes: Individuals with SSADHD may develop exertional dyskinesia, typically in late adolescence or early adulthood
checklist.why: Age-dependent movement disorder the review singles out (Statement 8).

checklist.name: hemiballismus
quotes: exertional dyskinesia, typically in late adolescence or early adulthood, with dystonic posturing or hemiballismus
checklist.why: Named late-onset movement disorder that distinguishes older patients.

checklist.name: autism spectrum disorder or autistic behaviors
quotes: ASD has an occurrence rate of ~50% in SSADHD
autistic behaviors such as problems with social communication and stereotypies
checklist.why: Core feature present in about half, emerging later with age.

checklist.name: attention problems or ADHD
quotes: sleep disturbances, attention problems, anxiety
first-line intervention for ADHD symptoms in SSADHD
checklist.why: Core neurobehavioral feature.

checklist.name: anxiety
quotes: attention problems, anxiety, and obsessive-compulsive traits
checklist.why: Core psychiatric feature.

checklist.name: obsessive-compulsive traits
quotes: anxiety, attention problems, obsessive-compulsive traits, and sleep disturbances
checklist.why: Core psychiatric feature.

checklist.name: aggression or disruptive behavior
quotes: seizures, disruptive behaviors, autistic behaviors
Behavioral difficulties such as defiance or aggression
checklist.why: Named among consistently reported behaviors and said to worsen with age.

checklist.name: sleep disturbances
quotes: obsessive-compulsive traits, and sleep disturbances
checklist.why: Core feature in the abstract, introduction, Statement 3 and conclusions.

checklist.name: depression or mood fluctuation
quotes: Anxiety, mood fluctuation, and obsessive-compulsive traits
SSRIs are efficacious and indicated for depression, anxiety, and OCD in individuals with SSADHD
checklist.why: Psychiatric feature the review discusses in adolescents and adults.

checklist.name: psychotic symptoms (hallucinations or delusions)
quotes: Hallucinations, delusions, and ideas of reference may be part of the clinical presentation of SSADHD
features associated with psychosis in individuals with SSADHD
checklist.why: Psychiatric feature reported in case reports; psychiatric features increase with age.

checklist.name: T2 hyperintensity of globus pallidus, subthalamic or dentate nuclei on MRI
quotes: The typical neuroimaging findings of SSADHD include magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) T2-weighted signal hyperintensities in the globus pallidi, subthalamic nuclei, and cerebellar dentate nuclei
checklist.why: The typical imaging finding, often reported in case reports.

checklist.name: cerebral or cerebellar atrophy
quotes: More rarely, other abnormalities, such as cortical and cerebellar atrophy, may be seen
checklist.why: Less common imaging finding the review names.

left_out: elevated urinary gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB): the diagnostic screening marker, present by definition
elevated GABA or GABA-related metabolites (CSF, plasma): diagnostic biomarker done only in specialized labs, near-defining
increased GABA/NAA ratio on MR spectroscopy: specialized test rarely reported in case reports
adaptive function deficits: overlaps intellectual disability; case reports seldom state it separately
movement disorders (as a broad item): split into ataxia, dystonia, exertional dyskinesia and hemiballismus to avoid overlap
stereotypies and social communication problems: kept inside the autism item rather than as separate items
cerebrovascular accident, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, hypothyroidism, strabismus: the review says these have no known association with the disorder (Statement 5)
symptom onset in the first year of life: an onset descriptor, not a phenotypic feature
notes: Source is a consensus guideline (Tokatly Latzer et al. 2024), not GeneReviews; its clinical description is a list of features without frequencies for most. Hemiballismus and psychotic symptoms are less established (psychosis has weak expert agreement, level C) but the review names them as part of the presentation; hemiballismus was chosen as the 20th item over MR spectroscopy and adaptive deficits. 'Depression or mood fluctuation' rests on Statement 28 (a treatment statement) that names these as occurring in individuals with SSADHD. Dystonia and exertional dyskinesia are separate items: the review lists dystonia as its own movement disorder, and exertional dyskinesia as an episodic, exercise-induced phenomenon.
